A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Oryx research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original image, video, and ScanQA evaluations, architecture ablations, retrieval experiments, and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds efficiency measurements, further ablations, qualitative comparisons, and failure cases.

M1.justification: OryxViT, variable-length attention, dynamic compression, the shared MLP, and the training procedure remain substantively unchanged. Appendix D.2 specifies previously underdocumented encoder pretraining; it does not establish a newly introduced procedure. The original compression settings remain in Appendix D.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite and established training-task coverage remain unchanged. Appendix B adds targeted qualitative scenarios involving timestamp-specific video description and chemical-knowledge reasoning. CapsFusion and synthesized OCR data are newly identified pretraining sources, without establishing that the underlying training coverage changed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their comparator sets. v3 adds LLaVA-OneVision responses to the four generation examples, separate image/video MLPs in Table 8, and standalone convolution and Q-former alternatives in Table 9(a). These extend supplementary comparisons without revising the main benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Retained benchmark protocols and main training settings are unchanged. New protocols include A100 throughput and memory measurements at 1280 × 1280 pixels, batch size four for the memory comparison, a square-image memory sweep, and controlled data/adapter comparisons. Separate MLPs are initialized from pretrained image weights.

E4.justification: Appendices B–C substantially expand analysis with explicit failure cases, efficiency and memory scaling, ablations separating long-video data, 3D data and coarse correspondences, shared versus separate adapters, and additional downsampling alternatives. The earlier resolution, compression, and needle-in-a-haystack analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the relocated retrieval heatmap retain their results. Substantial new findings include OryxViT/SigLIP throughput of 146.5/157.7 images per second and memory of 49.1/48.7 GB, training-data ablation scores, and shared/separate MLP MLVU scores of 59.3/54.2. Qualitative outputs and failures are also added; the tennis caption is replaced. Table 9(b) repeats existing results.

T1.justification: The native-resolution construction and cross-attention equation are retained, with no new proofs, derivations, or theoretical results. Generalized compression-ratio wording does not change the documented implementation or establish a substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, central introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about native-resolution encoding, dynamic compression, unified spatial-temporal understanding, and competitive performance. New appendix evidence supports existing claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning temporal localization and chemical-knowledge reasoning, with proposed causes and remedies in Appendix B. Appendices A and C also introduce interpretations of hallucination, memory overhead, shared-adapter feature distributions, and fixed-token Q-former limitations. These substantially broaden the account of applicability and mechanisms, although several explanations remain hypotheses.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 fills a substantial encoder-pretraining documentation gap: Qwen2-0.5B, LoRA, 0.6B trainable parameters, 400M pretraining examples, CapsFusion/synthesized OCR sources, batch size 2048, and cross-entropy loss are specified. Existing main training details are relocated unchanged. The earlier explicit maximum positional-embedding size is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds Insight-V (Dong et al., 2024) in the introduction and CapsFusion (Yu et al., 2024) for encoder-pretraining data. The related-work discussion and central positioning against previous approaches remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose is retained. Bounded structural edits regroup data curation under Section 3.2, move implementation details and the retrieval experiment into appendices, place references after the appendices, and update the publication header. Added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with Tables 6–9, two failure-case figures, and a memory curve. Existing generation panels incorporate baseline answers and colored emphasis. The original retrieval heatmap moves from Figure 3 to Figure 10, and the resolution plot becomes Figure 3; both retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v2: efficiency claims gain direct measurements, curated training data and adapter choices gain targeted ablations, and encoder pretraining receives essential technical documentation. Explicit failure cases also clarify limits missing from the earlier success-focused examples. Together these substantially strengthen evidential support and transparency while preserving the main results, outweighing the limited loss of positional-embedding size detail.
